articles.title: The 'Big One' Might Not Come Alone: Two West Coast Faults Could Strike Together
articles.summary: A new study says the Cascadia and San Andreas faults may sometimes rupture within minutes or hours of each other. Scientists found evidence in 3,100 years of ocean sediment. If both go off, cities like Seattle, Portland, and San Francisco could all need help at once.

articles.title: Black Holes of Every Size Follow the Same Surprising Rule
articles.summary: Astronomers found that black holes — from small ones to giant ones — launch powerful jets at the same stage of their feeding cycle. They studied stars being torn apart to catch black holes in the act. The rule kicks in when feeding drops to about 2% of a key limit.

articles.title: Seals Are Secret Ocean Scientists!
articles.summary: Imagine a seal with a tiny computer on its head, diving deep under Antarctic ice. That's real! Oceanographer Lily Dove used seal data to study how the Southern Ocean is warming.
